implementation.note: CPU graph planning and actual Metal pixel readback exercised.

architecture.note: PRISMA owns the screen-space chain; named resources and pass dependencies compile through the existing render graph. Camera inputs flow through the existing LENS target pool.

native_api.note: Validated compiler, view-scoped texture inputs and view pass counts.

skill.note: Recipe for masked camera glow and acceptance.

mcp.note: The compiled MCP registry contains both operations. Fresh stdio processes read the saved graph and reject invalid or stale writes.

studio.note: The production React PostFxPanel saved a custom threshold through studio.op and reloaded it in Chromium against native MCP.

inspector.note: Loaded the glow example in the panel, confirmed invalid JSON disables saving, changed the threshold, saved and reloaded the three passes.

persistence.note: Verified the game graph on disk after process restart. A map override, explicit disable and inheritance survived independent save/reopen cycles.

graphs.note: Verified pass sorting, aliasing, rejection of invalid graphs and staged Metal/WebGL dispatch.

performance.note: Measured a 4-pass 640x320 graph against a zero-pass baseline including readback. Resource bindings use fixed arrays capped at 12 passes and eight camera inputs. Reused targets are keyed by plan slot and resolution.

platforms.note: Actual rendering exercised on macOS Metal and Chromium WebGL2. Other RHI paths are unverified.

dependencies.note: Compiled demo using existing GfxGL, Shader Graph, JSON and PRISMA sources; no new runtime dependency.

headless.note: GPU-free compositor compilation and validation exercised via the native data test.

examples.note: Saved game/map postfx block with a masked-camera glow example.

tests.note: Native x86_64 Metal pixel comparison of four 96x64 frames. CPU topology/validation test separately run. Full suite and other backends pending.

handoff.note: Implementation SHA and verification limits recorded.

documentation.note: Document schema, resource lifetimes and entry points.

publishing.note: Bilingual site entry, real WebGL capture and interactive WebAssembly demo built and exercised on Chromium; deployment follows main integration.
